value: IC06 mixing coefficients were significantly higher in AUD patients than in healthy controls.
IC06 involved a widespread gray-matter pattern and multiple commissural, projection, and associative white-matter fibers.
The regions included in IC06 were interpreted as more tightly related to neural changes associated with chronic alcohol consumption than IC08.

spans.text: While mixing coefficients of IC06 and IC11 were higher in patients compared with controls [IC06:   t  (38) = −5.69,   p   < 0.001; IC11:   t  (38) = −3.82,   p   < 0.001], IC08 displayed the opposite pattern [IC08:   t  (38) = 5.17,   p   < 0.001]. IC06 involved a widespread GM pattern encompassing the sensorimotor cortex and supplementary motor area, cingulate cortex, and precuneus, subcortical nuclei (bilateral thalamus, left caudate), plus an extensive sector of the occipital cortex (calcarine cortex, cuneus, lingual gyrus), and bilateral cerebellum (crus II). The distribution of DTI indices for this component involved commissural (body of corpus callosum and forceps major), projections (bilateral anterior thalamic radiation and superior corona radiata, as well as the right cerebral peduncle), and associative (fornix plus stria terminalis, as well as the posterior sectors of bilateral superior and inferior longitudinal fasciculi, inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus and cingulum bundle) fibers ( Figure 1 ).

We then carried out DTI group analyses with Tract-Based Spatial Statistics (TBSS) ( Smith et al., 2006 ), involving a voxelwise non-linear registration of all participants’ fractional anisotropy (FA) maps that, once aligned, are affine-transformed on a standard space (1 mm × 1 mm × 1 mm MNI152).

value: IC08 mixing coefficients were significantly lower in AUD patients than in healthy controls.
IC08 was represented by a subcortical gray-matter pattern including the bilateral amygdala and left hippocampus, together with a widespread white-matter pattern.
The opposite pattern for IC08, compared with IC06 and IC11, suggested a weaker contribution of its regions to neural changes associated with chronic alcohol consumption.

spans.text: IC08 was represented by a subcortical GM pattern including bilateral amygdala and left hippocampus, and by a widespread DTI pattern primarily involving all sectors of corpus callosum (genu, body, and splenium), forceps minor and forceps major, anterior thalamic radiations and cerebral peduncles, the anterior limb of internal capsule and the fornix (body and column) ( Figure 2 ).

We then carried out DTI group analyses with Tract-Based Spatial Statistics (TBSS) ( Smith et al., 2006 ), involving a voxelwise non-linear registration of all participants’ fractional anisotropy (FA) maps that, once aligned, are affine-transformed on a standard space (1 mm × 1 mm × 1 mm MNI152).

source_definition.value: Lifetime duration of alcohol abuse, obtained from a semi-structured interview about drinking history.

spans.text: AUD patients underwent a semi-structured interview conducted by an expert clinician about their drinking history, including the type, the amount, and lifetime duration of alcohol use.

model_settings.value: Five feature datasets (GM density, FA, AD, MD, and RD) were normalized to equal average sum-of-square and combined in a participant × feature matrix. PCA reduced dimensionality to 12 ICs using the minimum description length criterion; Infomax decomposed the matrix; the jICA was repeated 50 times in Icasso and clustered for stability. Mixing coefficients were compared between groups using two-sample t-tests with Bonferroni-adjusted significance threshold p = 0.004.
